thread:
Nina: heads up — noticing a weird limiter behavior in prod since 03:41 UTC, some tenants getting sudden 429s while others see no change. suspected burst refill anomaly.
Alex: which limiter? global shard or per-tenant? any tenant ids?
Nina: per-tenant token-bucket on the api-gateway path (/v1/generate). affected tenants: t-4821, t-9002 (both heavy embedding users). rate metrics show short spikes in available_tokens followed by immediate refills.
Julian: can you paste the metrics? bucket rate / refill_unit?
Nina: paste logs + metric snippet:
```
# metric series (shortened)
limiter.available_tokens{tenant=t-4821} 0 -> 2400 -> 0 -> 2400  (1s cadence)
limiter.refill_rate{tenant=t-4821} 2400
config: refill_amount=2400, refill_unit=1  <-- suspicious
```
Nina: note: refill_unit is set to 1 (we store unit as seconds normally) but the recent rollout touched the config schema for Dedicated tenants. looks like a unit mismatch (ms vs s) in the new setter.
sre-oncall: @Nina can you confirm whether the change landed in config-service? who's the author of that PR?
Nina: PR #4823 by @maria (config-service). change was to accept arbitrary dt strings and normalize. I grep'd state and saw pre-normalized values persisted: refill_unit=1 (int) — the code path for dedicated conversions treats that as milliseconds.
Julian: that would mean refill every 1ms -> insane token generation -> burst pump then throttle logic triggers 429? explain timeline.
Nina: timeline: 03:39 internal deploy (config-service v1.12.4), 03:41 first spikes, 03:44 alerts from support about client 429s. many clients then hit token exhaustion because gateway sees rapid refill->fast consumption pattern and our fairness heuristics kick in dropping requests for other tenants.
Alex: support reported a high-severity customer complaint (t-4821). They provided repro: steady 8 req/s before, after change many small bursts and elevated latency.
sre-oncall: mitigation actions queued?
Julian: immediate mitigation: rollback config normalization to previous behavior for dedicated tenants (rolled at 03:52). also pushed a hotfix to treat bare ints as seconds explicitly (hotfix #4827).
Nina: rollback confirmed — metrics improved after 03:55. tokens stabilized to correct refill cadence (1 token/sec equivalents). no data loss but some customers saw 429s for ~13 minutes.
Alex: support note prepared. asked for root cause and mitigation ETA.
Julian: planned follow-ups: 1) add validation on config write to reject ambiguous units, 2) add canary check to detect refill_rate anomalies (alert if refill_rate > baseline * 10), 3) add a migration script to normalize existing persisted values.
sre-oncall: also add a synthetic tenant in staging that pumps config variations to catch future schema regressions.
Nina: repro steps we used in staging (for oncall to reproduce quickly):
1. start local config-service with branch maria/config-normalize
2. create tenant stub with refill_amount=2400, refill_unit=1
3. hit the gateway endpoint with an embedded load generator: `wrk -t2 -c50 -d60s http://staging-gateway/v1/generate?tenant=t-stub`
4. observe `limiter.available_tokens` where tokens jump/reset every 1s or faster (depending on unit interpretation)
Julian: log snippet from server at 03:42 showing conversion path: 
```
2026-03-11T03:42:12Z config-service INFO apply: tenant=t-4821 refill_amount=2400 refill_unit=1 incoming_unit=ms interpreted_unit=ms
2026-03-11T03:42:12Z limiter WARN fast-refill detected tenant=t-4821 computed_refill_rate=2400000/s
```
Nina: root cause summary (short): config normalization PR introduced ambiguous parsing of numeric units — bare ints were treated as milliseconds for dedicated tenants. persisted configs with unit-less ints caused excessive refill rates.
Alex: customer-facing summary (for support): we had a configuration bug in an internal service that briefly caused our rate limiter to generate tokens far faster than intended. this caused transient 429s and elevated latency for some customers. we rolled back the change and applied a hotfix; service is stable.
Julian: next-owner assignments: 
- config validation + migration: Julian (due 2026-03-18)
- alerts + synthetic: Nina (due 2026-03-16)
- postmortem doc + exec summary: Alex (due 2026-03-17)
sre-oncall: retrospective action: add an integration test for unit parsing in config-service with persisted state. cc @deploy-bot please tag releases touched by PR #4823/4827 for traceability.
deploy-bot: noted — releases tagged: config-service@v1.12.4 (bad), config-service@v1.12.5-hotfix (rolled).
Nina: one more thing — audit DB queries showed ~12 tenants had ambiguous unit ints; I'll kick off normalization job and include a dry-run report in the postmortem.
Alex: thanks all — I'll update the customer thread and mark support escalation resolved after PM review. :white_check_mark:
